videos.title: Spirit Airlines Went Bankrupt Twice in Six Months — Then Vanished Completely
videos.description:
Spirit Airlines was once one of America's most recognizable budget carriers — bright yellow planes, rock-bottom fares, and millions of loyal (and frustrated) flyers. Then, in the span of about eighteen months, it filed for bankruptcy twice and completely ceased operations. This is the full story of how a blocked $3.8 billion merger with JetBlue, a failed Frontier deal, a surging jet fuel market, and years of unresolved losses combined to end one of the biggest names in U.S. discount aviation. We break down the real timeline — from the first Chapter 11 filing in November 2024, to the brief 2025 emergence, to the second bankruptcy, to the final Chapter 7 liquidation in May 2026 — and explain exactly why this wasn't a simple restructuring, but a total collapse.

Sources referenced include CNBC, Skift, and industry financial trackers covering Spirit's bankruptcy filings and wind-down costs.

videos.title: 7-Eleven Is Closing 645 Stores — Is It Over?
videos.description: 7-Eleven is one of the most recognizable retail brands in America — but its own numbers tell a different story than its storefronts do. In fiscal 2026, the chain plans to close 645 North American locations while opening only 205, marking the fifth straight year it has closed more stores than it opened. Meanwhile parent company Seven & i Holdings is projecting a 9.4% revenue decline. In this episode of The Business Flow, we break down what's verified fact, what's strategic pivot, and what remains a genuinely open question about 7-Eleven's future. This is not a bankruptcy claim — it's a documented look at real financial and operational pressure. Watch, then tell us what you think happens next.

videos.title: America's Richest Family: The Walton $520 Billion Fortune Explained
videos.description: America's richest family isn't a mystery brand or an obscure dynasty — it's the Waltons, of Walmart. But the real story behind their estimated $520 billion fortune isn't about low prices. It's about a structural decision that let one family's wealth compound for over sixty years without being diluted away like so many other dynasties. In this episode we verify the numbers, separate company value from family net worth, and reveal the ownership mechanism that made this the largest family fortune in the United States.

videos.title: 5 Companies That Secretly Run the Internet, Your Phone, and Your Car
videos.description: Five companies you rarely think about are quietly holding up the modern world -- from the cloud servers running your bank and hospital apps, to the chip factories in Taiwan, to one machine-maker in the Netherlands that almost nobody outside the semiconductor industry can name. This is not a conspiracy story. It's a factual look at concentration, complexity, and why a handful of companies became structurally irreplaceable. We break down AWS, Microsoft, and Google's grip on cloud infrastructure spending, TSMC's outsized role in global chip manufacturing, and the one equipment maker whose machines make advanced chipmaking possible in the first place -- saved for the reveal at the end.

videos.title: SpaceX: The $62 Million Rocket That Broke the Space Industry
videos.description: For decades, launching anything into orbit was one of the most expensive things a government or company could do. Then SpaceX showed up with an idea the industry called impossible: land the rocket, refuel it, and fly it again. This episode breaks down exactly how that bet rewired the economics of spaceflight — from $200 million throwaway rockets to a reusable Falcon 9 that now flies for a fraction of the price, and why that shift is still locking legacy competitors out of the market. Sourced from verified industry cost analyses and case studies referenced in the episode.

videos.title: America's Richest Company in 2026? Amazon, Nvidia and Alphabet All Claim It
videos.description: Amazon just ended Walmart's 13-year reign atop the Fortune 500 with $715 billion in revenue. Nvidia is worth $5.58 trillion, more than any company on Earth — despite ranking just 16th in sales. And Alphabet quietly out-earns them both with $244 billion in pure profit. So which one is really America's richest company? This episode breaks down revenue, market value, and profit as three separate scoreboards, shows why each one crowns a different winner, and reveals the reversal hiding at the top of the profit rankings. Sourced from 2026 Fortune 500 and market cap data.

videos.title: NVIDIA, Apple & Alphabet: The Hidden Business Behind the 3 Biggest Companies on Earth (2026)
videos.description: In September 2026, three American companies are worth a combined total north of fourteen trillion dollars — and none of them got there for the reason most people assume. This episode ranks the three largest U.S. companies by market capitalization and unpacks the real economic engine hiding behind each familiar brand: the search company that's really an AI infrastructure landlord, the phone company that's really a services subscription machine, and the graphics-card company that quietly became the most valuable company on Earth. We define the ranking metric, explain why it matters for anyone with a 401k or index fund, and save the #1 reveal for the end.

videos.title: 5 U.S. Companies Behind More of the Market Than You Realize (#5 Isn't Who You Think)
videos.description: Five U.S. companies are quietly pouring $660–$690 billion into the infrastructure behind your everyday apps, searches, and streams in 2026 alone — nearly double what they spent the year before. This episode breaks down exactly how Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Digital Realty measurably shape the internet's physical backbone through cloud market share, leased data center power, and capital spending — then reveals the one company almost nobody thinks about that every single one of them depends on to keep building at all: Micron. No conspiracy claims, just verified capex numbers, market share data, and supply-chain bottlenecks straight from company guidance and industry reports.

videos.title: The 5 Most Valuable U.S. Companies in 2026 — NVIDIA's Hidden Money Machine Beats Apple
videos.description: In September 2026, five U.S. companies are worth a combined $20+ trillion — and almost none of that value comes from the products they're famous for. This episode ranks the five most valuable American public companies by market capitalization and breaks down the real business mechanism behind each valuation: Amazon's cloud backend hiding behind e-commerce, Microsoft's AI infrastructure hiding behind Windows and Office, Alphabet's advertising engine hiding behind search, Apple's services ecosystem hiding behind the iPhone, and finally NVIDIA — the former gaming chip company that became the world's most valuable company by supplying the compute power the entire AI economy runs on. All figures are approximate market capitalizations as of September 2026 based on cited market data sources.

videos.title: Meta's $1,300 Glasses Just Made a Billion-Dollar Bet on Your Face
videos.description:
Meta just announced its new VR glasses for $1,300. Weighing just 100 grams, packed with 5K micro-OLED displays, and powered by an external compute puck, this device promises to replace every screen in your daily life — from your TV to your workspace monitors.

In this video from The Business Flow, we break down the business strategy behind the launch, the engineering breakthroughs, the real limitations (like the 3-hour battery life), and whether spatial computing can truly replace our smartphones and PCs.
